cover: Technical debt, explained for the people who pay

slides.title: You pay it as interest
slides.body: Every new feature takes longer and breaks more than it would in a cleaner system.

slides.title: Spot it without reading code
slides.body: Small changes take weeks, releases break unrelated things, and one person holds the knowledge.

slides.title: A full rewrite is rarely the first move
slides.body: It freezes new work for months, and the new system has to rediscover every rule the old one handled.

slides.title: Start where it hurts
slides.body: Debt in code nobody touches costs almost nothing. Debt in the checkout flow costs you every week.

slides.title: Budget for it every cycle
slides.body: Clean up what each feature touches and reserve time for upgrades, so the work happens before it's urgent.
